title: Confirm RMS-to-OptiSweep communication uses REST API (and avoid bypassing OptiSweep software)
summary: When investigating an issue between the RMS and OptiSweep, treat the communication path as API-based—specifically REST API—and avoid sending requests in a way that bypasses the OptiSweep software flow. Bypassing OptiSweep software can leave OptiSweep unaware of the transaction (no knowledge of the database of that transaction), which can lead to out-of-sync behavior.
when_to_use: Use this when a support call involves an issue “between RMS and OptiSweep” and you need to frame the communication boundary correctly (REST API integration) and ensure you do not bypass OptiSweep software in a way that can desynchronize transaction visibility.
not_for: Do not use this as a step-by-step guide to perform direct/bypassing API transactions outside the documented OptiSweep software flow (the source explicitly warns against bypassing).

Do not use this to obtain concrete request/response field mappings for REST calls; the source only points to where the API spec lives (Confluence) and does not provide field-level troubleshooting steps.
roles_and_responsibilities: L2_support: Use the RMS↔OptiSweep boundary guidance to explain the correct integration model (REST API) and to prevent bypass actions that can cause out-of-sync behavior.
L2_support: If API specifications are needed, use the documented API spec location on Confluence for both RMS and Geek Plus.
safety_notes: Avoid bypassing OptiSweep software flow when sending API requests; the source warns this can cause OptiSweep to be unaware of the transaction and lead to out-of-sync behavior.

Confluence access to the API spec for both RMS and Geek Plus
Awareness of REST API / Geek Plus API usage (as referenced by the segment)

steps.title: Do not bypass OptiSweep software flow when considering direct REST/API requests
steps.purpose: Prevent out-of-sync transaction visibility caused by bypassing OptiSweep software.
steps.instruction: If you are considering sending requests directly (e.g., via Geek Plus API / REST API), verify that you are not bypassing the OptiSweep software flow. The segment warns that bypassing OptiSweep software can leave OptiSweep unaware of what happened and without knowledge of the database of that transaction.
steps.expected_result: You stop or avoid bypass actions and instead keep the OptiSweep software flow as the authoritative path for transactions.
steps.healthy_condition: Any API usage you plan is consistent with the idea that OptiSweep software is “in charge,” and you do not create a scenario where OptiSweep has no knowledge of the transaction.
steps.failure_condition: You proceed with bypassing OptiSweep software such that OptiSweep does not know what happened (no knowledge of the database of that transaction), creating out-of-sync behavior.
